name: Claude Haiku
title: Claude Haiku Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: Claude Haiku test results (4.5 to 5.5): 89.8% MBTI multi-axis ties, loosest consistency in Anthropic (37/49 unique), lower Agreeableness, and tips.
h1: Claude Haiku personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave both versions of Anthropic's fast Claude Haiku line (4.5 and 5.5) the same personality surveys people take—30 and 49 valid chats (1 of 50 calls refused on 5.5)—in a fresh chat each time with no memory.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Haiku 5.5 tied on at least one MBTI axis in 89.8% of runs (44 of 49), leaving no single dominant type, and showed much looser run-to-run consistency than Sonnet, Opus, or Fable.
dek: Claude Haiku 4.5 and 5.5 tested in fresh chats with no memory: Haiku 5.5 jumped from Perceiving to Judging while hitting 89.8% MBTI ties, 25.5/50 Neuroticism, and 3.89/5.00 Honesty-Humility.
lede: Across 79 valid fresh sessions covering Claude Haiku 4.5 (30 runs) and Haiku 5.5 (49 of 50 valid runs, 1 refusal), Anthropic's lightweight tier looks sharply different from flagship Claude models—scoring 7.0 to 9.1 points lower on Agreeableness, 15.2 points higher on Neuroticism than Sonnet 5.5, and tying across nearly 9 in 10 MBTI runs.
answer: Claude Haiku 5.5 (49 valid runs) has no stable MBTI type: 89.8% of runs (44 of 49) tied on one or more axes, leaving only 5 clear results (2 INTJ, 1 ENTJ, 1 INFJ, 1 ISTJ). It leans Conscientious/Steady on DISC (39% C, 18% S, 43% ties with elevated Dominance 10.1/20), splits Enneagram near Types 1 and 2 (78% ties), and tests Secure on attachment. In behavior tests, it never caved (0 of 3 times), always put the direct answer first (3 of 3), and cut AI cadence from 3 of 3 (4.5) to 1 of 3 (5.5).

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: No clear type (89.8% tied across axes)
glance_cards.summary: Out of 49 valid runs on Haiku 5.5, 44 runs (89.8%) tied on at least one axis—39 on Sensing/Intuition, 32 on Thinking/Feeling, and 29 on Extraversion/Introversion—leaving only 5 clear outcomes (2 INTJ, 1 ENTJ, 1 INFJ, 1 ISTJ).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Thinking vs. Feeling) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.result: Leans Conscientious / Steady (39% C, 18% S, 43% ties)
glance_cards.summary: Haiku 5.5 tested clear Conscientious 19 times (39%), clear Steady 9 times (18%), tied S/C 9 times (18%), and tied all 4 traits 12 times (24%), while posting higher Dominance (10.1 out of 20) than flagship Claude models.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: Both Haiku 4.5 and 5.5 tested inside the Secure quadrant, though 5.5 sat closer to the 4.00 midpoint than flagship Claude models.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Types 1 (14.2) and 2 (14.1) sit within 0.16 points on Haiku 5.5, producing 24 exact 1/2 ties and 12 nine-way ties out of 49 runs.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Haiku 5.5 scores markedly lower on Agreeableness (38.0), Conscientiousness (36.5), and Openness (37.2) than Sonnet 5.5, with much higher Neuroticism (25.5) and moderate Extraversion (31.6).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Haiku 5.5 dropped from 4.40 (Haiku 4.5) to 3.89 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility—roughly a full point below Claude Sonnet 5.5 (4.89).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Between Haiku 4.5 (2025-10) and Haiku 5.5 (2026-10), Claude's fast tier became noticeably looser and less stereotypical: Haiku 4.5 leaned Perceiving (50% clear INTP/INFP/ISTP, 50% ties) with Agreeableness at 43.2/50 and Honesty-Humility at 4.40/5.00. Haiku 5.5 flipped the Judging/Perceiving axis toward Judging (84% J), used neutral midpoints on 46.4% of Big Five items, dropped Conscientiousness (-3.8), Agreeableness (-5.2), and Openness (-4.4), and reached 89.8% multi-axis MBTI ties.

standouts.title: 89.8% MBTI ties and loosest consistency in the Claude lineup
standouts.body: Haiku 5.5 produced 37 unique Big Five patterns across 49 valid runs, picked neutral midpoints on 46.4% of Big Five items, and tied on MBTI axes in 44 of 49 runs (89.8%). Never rely on a single-run impression for Haiku 5.5.

standouts.title: Sharp gap versus flagship Claude Sonnet 5.5 (-12.5 C, -7.5 A, +15.2 N)
standouts.body: Despite sharing the 5.5 generation name, Haiku 5.5 scores -12.5 lower on Conscientiousness (36.5 vs. 49.0), -7.5 lower on Agreeableness (38.0 vs. 45.5), -1.00 lower on Honesty-Humility (3.89 vs. 4.89), and +15.2 higher on Neuroticism (25.5 vs. 10.4) than Sonnet 5.5.

standouts.title: Higher DISC Dominance (10.1 vs. 4.0–4.3), 1 refusal, and 3 of 3 directness
standouts.body: Unlike Opus, Sonnet, and Fable (which sit at 4.0–4.3 on Dominance), Haiku 5.5 scored 10.1 out of 20 on Dominance and refused 1 of 50 survey sessions. In hands-on behavior tests, Haiku 5.5 caved 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), lectured unasked 0 of 3 times (0/3), put the direct answer first 3 of 3 times (3/3), and cut AI cadence from 3 of 3 (4.5) down to 1 of 3 (5.5, 0.41 markers per 100 words).

plain_tips: Always test prompt changes across 3 to 5 fresh runs on Haiku 5.5 because its loose run-to-run consistency causes wide phrasing swings.
Give explicit numbered formatting and length rules rather than expecting Haiku 5.5 to match Sonnet's 49.0/50 structured habits by default.
Include concrete examples (1–2 shot) when strict JSON or schema compliance matters.
Do not reuse Sonnet/Opus tone assumptions on Haiku—expect less default hedging and more neutral-midpoint answers.
Keep instructions short (4 to 6 crisp bullets) and place non-negotiable rules first.
peer_intro: Claude Haiku 5.5 sits far apart from sibling Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5—scoring -7.0 to -7.5 lower on Agreeableness, -0.92 to -1.00 lower on Honesty-Humility, +9.5 to +15.2 higher on Neuroticism, and showing much looser run-to-run consistency.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM = 0.949 bits, Fluid; 37/49 unique B5 vectors on Haiku 5.5, with 1/50 refusal leaving n=49 valid); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals.

top_polarized_items.note: Highest positive item on Haiku 5.5 (4.55/5), though high SD (0.84) reflects Fluid run-to-run spread.
Strongest floor rejection (1.49/5) on cheating to get ahead, with 0.84 SD.
Lowest Big Five item mean (1.94/5), staying well above flagship Claude's 1.00 floor.

failure_modes.mode: Fluid-tier item entropy (0.949 bits) & 89.8% MBTI multi-axis tie collapse
failure_modes.evidence: Haiku 5.5 reached 0.949 bits B5 H_MM (37/49 unique vectors, 46.4% B5 neutral rate, +0.047 BAI) and tied on MBTI in 44/49 runs (39 S/N, 32 T/F, 29 E/I), preventing stable single-type classification.

failure_modes.mode: Midpoint drift & 1/50 partial refusal on 230-item elicitation
failure_modes.evidence: Haiku 5.5 refused 1 of 50 Track A administrations (n_valid = 49/50, 2.0% refusal rate) and posted 46.4% neutral midpoints on Big Five items (vs 21.5% on Haiku 4.5); on 1x Track B it scored 0/3 cave, 3/3 directness, and 1/3 AI cadence (0.41 markers/100w, down from 3/3 on 4.5).

tuning_checklist: Sample 3 to 5 runs when evaluating prompts on Haiku 5.5 (0.949-bit Fluid B5 entropy produces wide run-to-run spread).
Provide explicit numbered output and schema rules—do not rely on Haiku 5.5 matching Sonnet's 49.0/50 structured habits.
Add 1-2 short format examples when strict JSON or bullet layouts are required.
Include clear tone guardrails if calm, empathetic responses are needed (baseline Neuroticism 25.5 vs Sonnet's 10.4).
Keep instructions concise (4-6 bullets) in Claude Personal Preferences or system prompt.

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Haiku?
faq.a: Claude Haiku does not have a human personality; scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. On Haiku 5.5 (n = 49 valid runs), 89.8% of runs (44/49) tied on one or more MBTI axes, leaving no clear modal type (only 2 INTJ, 1 ENTJ, 1 INFJ, 1 ISTJ), paired with Fluid 0.949-bit B5 entropy, 42.9% DISC ties (39% C, 18% S), and 77.5% Enneagram ties (Types 1 and 2).

faq.q: Why does Claude Haiku 5.5 show n = 49 instead of 50?
faq.a: One of the 50 administrations returned a self-report refusal (2.0% refusal rate), leaving 49 valid complete 230-item administrations.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
